correctness.rationale: For N even≥4, R over F₂ has kernel K=span(e_even,e_odd), and imR=K⊥. As P is invertible, rank T=N−2 and im T=P K⊥. The restriction of the pairing (v,w)→〈v,Pw〉 to K has B=[[q,q+m],[q+m,q]] over F₂, m=N/2 modulo two. Hence dim(kerT∩imT)=2−rankB and rank T²=N−4+rankB. When m odd det B=1 and rankT²=N−2; when m even B is all-q and rankT²=N−3 or N−4. Equal first/second images make T bijective on im T, yielding exactly 2^(N−2) periodic states and three times as many preperiod-one states, with four total inverse images per periodic state. For N divisible by four, dim(ker T∩im T)=2−q counts zero-Jordan blocks of size≥2; no full later-transient claim. Counting prefix rotations yields q=1 iff r≡2,3 mod4. Independent actual F₂ matrix computation checked 3744 small permutations including all N=4,6, first 3000 N=8. The universal conclusion follows from the two-by-two pairing identity, not finite sampling.

value.rationale: The motivating permutation-XOR automata study explicitly leaves even ring lengths outside its direct-basin theorem. The exact parity-incidence phase split across every possible wiring answers a natural general dynamical boundary: whether the first image is already periodic and, if not, the number of unavoidable nilpotent modes. The result has a nontrivial all-permutation statement and finite-state census; it is not merely a rank calculation for one chosen P.
